Subject: Questions on token metering / rounding for PoC

Hi Evelyn,

We're getting started on a small PoC for patient visit summarization. Before we lock in the test environment, procurement asked for clarity on a few metering points so we can forecast cost. Could you confirm the following?

1) Do you charge for both input (prompt/history) and output (completion)? If so, is the context (chat history) always included in the billed input tokens or only the portion sent in the request?

2) What is your billing granularity / rounding rule? E.g., do you bill per token, per 64/100/1k token increments, or by request? If there are minimums we need to know how these apply.

3) For continuous sessions where we keep a rolling context (user + assistant history), is there a separate session-level minimum or do you only charge when we actually send tokens over the wire?

4) Any worked examples you can share so procurement can reconcile line items with expected usage?

If it's easiest, a one-page explainer + a CSV example with numbers would be perfect. We're targeting a mid-Feb pilot and procurement needs this to finalize the SOW.

Thanks,
Tim Russell
Head of NLP Engineering
BrightHealth AI

Eve / Karthik — here's a concise breakdown we can share (I attached a CSV + the proposed pricing workbook). High level: we charge for tokens processed by the model (request + response). Below are the specifics and a few examples you can paste into procurement.

How tokens are counted
- Input tokens = all tokens included in the request payload (system, user messages, any history you include).
- Output tokens = tokens generated by the model in the response.
- Total billed tokens = input tokens + output tokens for that request. Session-level history that is not sent in a request (e.g., stored on your side or cached at the client) is not billed unless you include it in the request.

Rounding & billing quantum
- Hosted (standard): metered in 64-token quanta. We round up each request's total billed tokens to the next multiple of 64.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): option to meter at 1-token granularity for customers who sign a committed throughput contract.
- Minimums: hosted customers see no monthly floor beyond actual usage; for pilot discounts we sometimes require a committed monthly minimum to qualify.

Worked examples (useful for procurement)
Example A – short summary request- Prompt: 430 tokens (system + user history included in request)- Completion: 1,270 tokens- Raw total = 430 + 1,270 = 1,700 tokens- Rounded (64-token quantum) = ceil(1700/64) * 64 = 27 * 64 = 1,728 tokens billed- If hosted rate = $0.000025 per token -> charge = 1,728 * $0.000025 = $0.0432
Example B – long-context follow-up where history is included- Prompt: 3,150 tokens (we include ~6 previous turns)- Completion: 600 tokens- Raw total = 3,150 + 600 = 3,750 tokens- Rounded = ceil(3750/64) * 64 = 59 * 64 = 3,776 tokens billed
Example C – dedicated per-token granularity (committed)- Prompt: 3,150 tokens- Completion: 600 tokens- Raw total = 3,750 tokens (no rounding)- If committed rate = $0.000018 per token -> charge = 3,750 * $0.000018 = $0.0675
Notes / edge cases- Caching: if you enable prefix/KV caching and the cached prefix is not sent as part of the request (i.e., reconstructed server-side) you are not billed for those tokens. If the full text of the prefix is sent as part of the request payload, it is billed.- Session windows: we do not apply a separate "session minimum" for hosted requests — only the per-request rounding quantum applies. For pilot discounts with a committed minimum, the minimum is applied at the account/month level.
Discounts & pilot commit- The 10% off hosted per-token list rate to qualify for pilot pricing is fine from a commercial perspective if Procurement agrees to a $25k/month minimum during the 3-month Pilot. That discount does not apply retroactively. We can codify this in the SOW and add a clause that if utilization exceeds committed minimum materially, we review step-down pricing.
Attachments included:
- proposed-pricing.xlsx (contains line-item math & discount tab)
- example-usage.csv (three session examples matching the ones above)
I'll send these to BrightHealth and copy you, Eve. LMK if you want a different rounding quantum for hosted (we've used 32/64 historically; 64 is current standard for new customers).
Thanks,

Thanks Aditya — this is exactly what procurement asked for. A couple quick clarifications:

1) The caching note is important. For our PoC we'll rely on server-side KV caching. Can you confirm this means we won't be billed for the cached prefix tokens if we only send a short key referencing the cache? (we want to avoid double charging)

2) The proposed 10% discount + $25k/month floor is acceptable in principle. Procurement wants that language in the SOW: explicit monthly committed minimum, discount applied to hosted per-token charges only, and a clause that unused committed dollars do not roll over. Is Redwood OK with that?

3) For planning, procurement asked if minimums are at the account level or per project. We have two product teams hitting the same account—they want to know if the $25k can be shared across projects.

If you can send the one-page explainer and the signed term sheet, we can move procurement.

Regards,
Tim

Tim — thanks for the quick read. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Caching confirmation: correct — server-side KV/prefix caching that is referenced by a short key and not materialized as text in the request will not be billed. We will include a brief technical addendum in the billing explainer to show the cache lookup flow so procurement can see exactly when tokens are charged.

2) Commercial terms: Redwood accepts the 10% hosted-rate discount tied to a $25k/month committed minimum for the 3-month Pilot. Key points we'll include in the SOW:
- Discount applies to hosted per-token charges only (not to Dedicated fees or add-on observability overages)
- Monthly committed minimum = $25,000, applied at the account level (see below on sharing)
- Unused committed dollars do not roll over and are not refundable
3) Account-level sharing: the $25k/month floor is applied at the Redwood account level and may be shared across projects under the same legal entity/tenant. If you need per-project isolation, we can discuss sub-accounting but that may change qualification for the pilot discount.
Next steps: Aditya will attach the one-page billing explainer and the example CSV; I'll ask Legal/Finance to produce the SOW language (we'll use deal id DH-2027-BH-089). If Procurement sends a preferred SOW template, please CC me and I'll expedite.
I'll attach a short PDF explainer for easy distribution.
